newsitem.title: ITALY: Benetton mulling buys, even Sportsystem.
newsitem.headline: Benetton mulling buys, even Sportsystem.

text.p: Italy's clothing group Benetton said it is carrying out "feasibility studies into a possible acquisition in sectors strategically coherent with the company's core business".
The statement was in a note distributed at Tuesday's annual shareholders' meeting at the group's headquarters in Ponzano.

It added that the studies, conducted with the aid of international investment banks, were also looking at Benetton Sportsystem, owned like the Benetton Group by the Benetton family's Edizione Holding, as one of the possible options for acquisition.

Analysts have said the financial market was concerned that Edizione could look to use Benetton's cash pile for its more financially stretched operations, such as Benetton Sportsystem, GS supermarkets and Autogrill.

Some have speculated Edizione might sell sports equipment company Benetton Sportsystem to Benetton group at an inflated price, but Benetton managing Director Carlo Gilardi said last month that this would not happen.
He told Reuters in an interview that if an acquisition was planned, the price of Benetton Sportsystem would be independently assessed.
Today's ordinary general meeting approved Benetton's previously announced 1996 accounts showing an 11.5 percent increase in net profit and the payment of 500 lire per share, up from 425 lire in 1995.
An EGM also approved the company's one for 25 share free capital increase and the already announced issue of bonds for a value up to 500 billion lire.
Benetton shares closed in Milan off 0.7 percent at 21,850 lire on a slightly firmer stock market.
